documents.name: Louvre Museum
documents.summary: The Louvre in Paris is a vast palace museum spanning ancient civilisations, Renaissance painting and many other collections.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Louvre in Paris is worth a deliberate museum visit for its depth and range, with major artworks and ancient collections gathered inside a palace.

coverImage.alt: Louvre palace wings and the glass entrance pyramid in Cour Napoléon at dusk.

documents.name: Puy du Fou
documents.summary: Puy du Fou in Les Epesses, France, is a historical spectacle park built around technically ambitious live performances.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Puy du Fou in Les Epesses rewards visitors who enjoy live spectacle with ambitious historical productions across a substantial park outing.

audience.notes: The live shows particularly suit children aged about six and older, teenagers and adults. Individual performances or activities may have stricter restrictions.

documents.name: Sentier Blanc-Martel
documents.summary: Sentier Blanc-Martel in France’s Verdon canyon is a full-day point-to-point hike through cliff paths, river-level sections, steep stairs and long tunnels.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Sentier Blanc-Martel in the Verdon rewards fit walkers with hours inside a large limestone canyon, moving between ledges, stairs, tunnels and river-level scenery.

customFacets.hiking.crowding: Very popular in summer; the official tourism office reports that traffic disperses after hikers enter the gorge, but shuttle capacity and narrow passages still reward advance planning.

legacy-best-season.label: Best season
legacy-best-season.note: Spring or autumn in dry stable weather; avoid July and August heat and winter rockfall conditions.

legacy-access-point.label: Access point
legacy-access-point.note: The route begins at Chalet de la Maline and ends at Point Sublime / the Visitor Center; the point-to-point day normally requires the reserved seasonal shuttle or a prearranged taxi.

variants.name: Chalet de la Maline to Point Sublime — current detour

importantCondition.description: Rockfall has closed the direct route from Couloir Samson to Point Sublime. Follow RD23A for about one kilometre, then GR49 to the Visitor Center. The detour includes about 0.84 km on live RD23A and a brief D952 section without confirmed pavement, so take care around traffic.

coverImage.alt: Turquoise Verdon River and limestone gorge viewed from Sentier Blanc-Martel in France.

documents.name: Aiguille du Midi
documents.summary: Aiguille du Midi above Chamonix, France, is a cable-car excursion to a 3,842-metre visitor complex with close views of Mont Blanc.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Aiguille du Midi above Chamonix offers close high-Alpine views from a cable-car-accessed complex, with the scale of Mont Blanc central to the reward.

legacy-indoor-state.label: High-mountain setting
legacy-indoor-state.note: The excursion combines outdoor high-altitude terraces with indoor passages; weather and altitude materially affect the visit.

coverImage.alt: The Mont Blanc massif viewed from Aiguille du Midi, 1 August 2026.

documents.name: Arc de Triomphe
documents.summary: The Arc de Triomphe in Paris combines monumental sculpture and memorial detail with a rooftop view along the city’s radiating avenues.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Arc de Triomphe in Paris is worth climbing for a city view shaped by radiating avenues, backed by monumental architecture and memorial details.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The visit includes climbing through the monument to its rooftop terrace; approach by the pedestrian underpass.

coverImage.alt: The Arc de Triomphe de l’Étoile in Paris, showing the central arch and sculptural reliefs.

documents.name: Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière
documents.summary: Notre-Dame de Fourvière in Lyon, France, is an ornate hilltop basilica with mosaics, chapels and broad views over the city.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Notre-Dame de Fourvière in Lyon pairs a richly decorated church interior with a hilltop panorama that helps place the city in its landscape.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: Enter the basilica for its mosaics, stonework and chapels, then use the outdoor esplanade for city views.

documents.name: Chartres en Lumières
documents.summary: Chartres en Lumières in France is a free evening walk among historic buildings, bridges and churches transformed by light and sound.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Chartres en Lumières makes the historic French city into a connected evening attraction, with illuminated architecture rewarding a walk across several sites.

coreExperience.note: The illuminated route is predominantly visual.

weather.label: Dress for a long outdoor evening
weather.note: Cold or rain can materially shrink the route.

2026-season.note: The announced programme runs nightly from 11 April 2026 to 3 January 2027.

coverImage.alt: Chartres Cathedral illuminated with colourful projections during Chartres en Lumières

documents.name: Cité de l’espace
documents.summary: Cité de l’espace in Toulouse, France, is a large space attraction with full-size hardware, interactive exhibits and planetarium experiences.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Cité de l’espace in Toulouse rewards space enthusiasts with real-scale equipment and several ways to explore the subject through activities and planetarium experiences.

audience.notes: The space exhibits particularly suit children aged about seven and older, teenagers and adults. Individual programmes may have stricter restrictions.

documents.name: Dune du Pilat
documents.summary: Dune du Pilat near La Teste-de-Buch, France, is a vast coastal sand ridge with views between the Atlantic and Landes pine forest.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Dune du Pilat near La Teste-de-Buch rewards the sand climb with an unusually large moving landscape and a panorama between ocean and pine forest.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The visit involves a demanding climb through sand to the dune crest.

coverImage.alt: The crest of the Dune du Pilat photographed on 30 July 2022.

documents.name: Eiffel Tower
documents.summary: The Eiffel Tower in Paris offers an ascent through its iron lattice structure to elevated views across the city.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Eiffel Tower in Paris combines a distinctive structural ascent with a broad city panorama, letting visitors experience the landmark’s scale from within.

documents.name: Futuroscope
documents.summary: Futuroscope near Poitiers, France, is a park built around media experiences, motion simulators and large spectacles.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Futuroscope near Poitiers offers a distinctive park outing through media, simulated movement and spectacle.

audience.notes: The attractions particularly suit children aged about seven and older, teenagers and adults. Individual simulators and activities may have stricter rules.

documents.name: Gouffre de Padirac
documents.summary: Gouffre de Padirac in southwest France combines a deep open chasm with a guided underground river boat journey and large cave chambers.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Gouffre de Padirac in France rewards a cave visit with an underground river boat section and immense chambers reached through a dramatic chasm.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The cave visit involves descending the chasm, walking underground and boarding a boat, so it requires more effort than a level outdoor viewpoint.

coverImage.alt: The open chasm and lift structure at the Gouffre de Padirac photographed on 9 August 2012.

documents.name: Hôtel des Invalides
documents.summary: Les Invalides in Paris combines a deep military-history museum with historic courtyards, the domed church and Napoleon’s monumental tomb.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Les Invalides in Paris gives a history visit substance through extensive military collections, with the Dome and Napoleon’s tomb adding a major architectural component.

coverImage.alt: An aerial view from the Eiffel Tower toward Les Invalides, its dome and western facade, photographed on 1 August 2015.

documents.name: Nausicaá Centre National de la Mer
documents.summary: Nausicaá in Boulogne-sur-Mer, France, is a very large aquarium and marine centre with immersive tank displays.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Nausicaá in Boulogne-sur-Mer stands out for large, immersive marine displays that make the tank design central to the visit.

audience.notes: The marine displays particularly suit children aged about five and older, teenagers and adults. Individual activities may have their own restrictions.

coverImage.alt: Nausicaá Centre National de la Mer visitor environment

documents.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
documents.summary: Notre-Dame in Paris is a reopened Gothic cathedral whose restored interior includes bright stonework, the nave, choir and side chapels.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Notre-Dame in Paris is worth an interior visit for the restored Gothic volume, bright stonework and chapels, which give the cathedral substance beyond its exterior.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The visit includes the restored cathedral interior, with nave, choir and side chapels; conservation may restrict parts of the site.

documents.name: Palace of Versailles
documents.summary: Versailles outside Paris combines the Hall of Mirrors and royal apartments with immense formal gardens and the wider Trianon estate.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Versailles near Paris rewards a planned day with concentrated French royal history, monumental interiors and gardens large enough to shape the whole outing.

visualSignals.label: Style
visualSignals.value: French Baroque · classical French palace architecture

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The estate visit includes palace interiors, with extensive gardens and Trianon adding outdoor walking.

coverImage.alt: An aerial view of the Palace of Versailles and its courtyards photographed on 19 August 2013.

documents.name: Palais Garnier
documents.summary: Palais Garnier in Paris is a richly decorated nineteenth-century opera house, rewarding for its staircase, gilded foyers and painted ceilings.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Palais Garnier in Paris is worth visiting for the richness of its staircase and foyers, with a complete architectural experience beyond attending an opera.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The daytime visit includes the opera house’s staircase and foyers; auditorium access depends on rehearsals and technical work.

coverImage.alt: Palais Garnier in Paris, showing its ornate south facade and gilded roof statues.

documents.name: Parc Astérix
documents.summary: Parc Astérix in Plailly, France, combines strong roller coasters, family rides and themed surroundings on a trip beyond Paris.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Parc Astérix near Paris gives families and coaster fans a varied ride day with enough themed character to make the park setting part of the appeal.

audience.notes: The rides particularly suit children aged about six and older through teenagers. Individual attractions may have stricter age or height rules.

documents.name: Sainte-Chapelle
documents.summary: Sainte-Chapelle in Paris is a medieval chapel whose upper room is surrounded by a near-continuous wall of thirteenth-century stained glass.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Sainte-Chapelle in Paris offers an unusually complete stained-glass interior, with daylight making the medieval windows the defining experience.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: Visit the lower chapel, then climb to the upper room to see its medieval stained glass.

documents.name: Basilica of Sacré-Cœur de Montmartre
documents.summary: Sacré-Cœur in Paris is Montmartre’s white hilltop basilica, combining a mosaic-rich interior with broad city views from its steps and esplanade.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Sacré-Cœur in Montmartre pairs a substantial church interior with one of Paris’s characteristic hilltop views, especially rewarding within a wider neighbourhood visit.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: Enter the basilica for its mosaic-rich interior, then use the steps and esplanade for city views.

documents.name: Millau Viaduct
documents.summary: The Millau Viaduct in southern France is a 2.46 km cable-stayed bridge, best understood from viewpoints above the Tarn valley.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Millau Viaduct in France combines exceptional engineering scale with a clear valley setting, giving viewpoint stops a reward beyond crossing the bridge.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: View the bridge from Aire du Viaduc and nearby outdoor viewpoints above the Tarn valley.

documents.name: Moulin Rouge
documents.summary: The Moulin Rouge in Paris presents a large cabaret revue of dance, elaborate costumes, stage effects and classic cancan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Moulin Rouge in Paris rewards a cabaret evening with polished ensemble dancing, elaborate costumes and memorable stage spectacle.

legacy-booking-advice.label: Booking advice
legacy-booking-advice.note: Advance booking is strongly advisable because performances are fixed-capacity.

documents.name: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace
documents.localName: Musée de l'Air et de l'Espace
documents.summary: The Air and Space Museum at Le Bourget outside Paris displays historic aircraft, Concordes, a Boeing 747 and space exhibits, with optional boarding access.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Air and Space Museum at Le Bourget rewards aviation interests with extensive real aircraft and opportunities to go beyond display cases through optional boarding.

legacy-accessibility-notes.label: Accessibility
legacy-accessibility-notes.note: The collection spans a very large site; some aircraft boarding and optional activities have separate access constraints.

documents.name: Panthéon
documents.summary: The Panthéon in Paris is a monumental mausoleum with a vast interior, dome and crypt containing important French figures.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Panthéon in Paris brings monumental architecture together with nationally important burials, making a focused visit for French history and civic memory.

legacy-access.label: Access
legacy-access.note: The visit includes the large interior and crypt with the burials of important French figures.

documents.name: Curie Museum
documents.summary: Musée Curie in Paris is a small free science-history museum in the original Curie laboratory complex, with rooms, instruments and documents.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Musée Curie in Paris makes a small visit rewarding through the original laboratory setting, connecting scientific history with the rooms and instruments where it developed.

documents.name: Palais-Royal Garden
documents.summary: The Palais-Royal Garden in Paris is a compact formal garden framed by historic arcades, offering a calm pause near the Louvre.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Palais-Royal Garden in Paris gives a nearby break a distinctive setting through formal planting and historic arcades.

legacy-indoor-state.label: Outdoor garden
legacy-indoor-state.note: Explore the outdoor garden and surrounding historic arcades.

coverImage.alt: The formal Jardin du Palais-Royal and flowering magnolia photographed in April 2005.

documents.name: Tuileries Garden
documents.summary: The Tuileries Garden in central Paris is a formal walking route between the Louvre and Concorde, with basins, sculptures and chairs for a pause.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The Tuileries Garden in Paris is worth using for a well-composed walk or rest, with water, sculpture and seating between major landmarks.

legacy-indoor-state.label: Outdoor garden
legacy-indoor-state.note: The visit is an outdoor walk or pause among the garden’s basins, sculptures and chairs.

coverImage.alt: The Jardin des Tuileries, its large octagonal basin and paths, photographed from above on 17 May 2018.
